questions.question: Explain how traditional fermentation practices evolved into modern industrial / fermentation techniques.
questions.solution_html:
• fermentation techniques.
  • (Traditional and modern ferementaion-(3 mark),Discoveries by Louis Pasteur-(1 mark))
  • Traditional fermentation began as a natural process using wild microorganisms for
  • making foods like curd, wine, and bread. Over time, people learned to control
  • conditions such as temperature and cleanliness to improve consistency. Scientic
  • discoveries by Louis Pasteur proved that microorganisms are responsible for
  • fermentation. This led to the isolation and use of specic microbial strains for beer
  • yield and quality. Modern industrial fermentation uses sterile conditions, controlled
  • pH, temperature, and oxygen in large bioreactors. It is now widely applied for
  • producing antibiotics, enzymes, alcohol, and other commercial products eciently.
questions.final_answer: producing antibiotics, enzymes, alcohol, and other commercial products eciently
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe how to prevent contamination during cheese aging.
questions.solution_html:
• (Pasteurized milk and hygiene-(2 mark),Temperature-(1 mark),sterilization-(1 mark))
  • Use high-quality pasteurized milk and maintain strict hygiene during handling.
  • Sterilize all equipment, aging rooms, and shelves before use.
  • Control temperature and humidity to optimal levels for proper ripening.
  • Limit exposure by handling cheese with clean tools and minimal contact.
  • Encourage benecial cultures to out-compete harmful microorganisms.
  • Regularly inspect cheeses and remove any contaminated or mold-infected samples
  • promptly.
questions.final_answer: promptly

questions.question: Differentiate between positive and negative selection techniques.
questions.solution_html:
• Dierentiate between positive and negative selection techniques.
  • Any 4 dierences with one example-(1mark) each
  • ●Positive selection allows growth of desired cells under selective conditions.
  • ● Negative selection eliminates unwanted cells while desired cells survive
  • ●Positive selection uses markers like antibiotic resistance
  • ●Negative selection uses toxic agents to kill specic cells
  • ●Positive selection directly identies transformed/recombinant cells
  • ●Negative selection removes non-recombinant or undesired cells
questions.final_answer: ●Negative selection removes non-recombinant or undesired cells
